text:
Marco T.: hey @people-ops, quick note — i get severe vertigo from the new build-alert strobe in the office (those red flash panels near the server alcove). when it goes off i can't safely reorient for a while. requesting: removal/relocation of strobe near my desk, temporary private office while we assess, and a written note in the accommodations ledger.
Aisha (Eng Manager): oh no, Marco — thanks for telling us. didn't realize signals were that strong. i can sign off on a temporary private desk and file the Facilities request. @Lina could you advise on documentation?
Lina (People Ops): Hi Marco — thanks for flagging and sorry you're dealing with this. Please submit the confidential accommodations form or DM me a brief functional summary (you can redact medical specifics). we'll open a case. in parallel Facilities can arrange a temporary private office and inspect/relocate the strobe.
peopleops-bot: Case created: AC-2040-901 by Lina (People Ops). Status: intake.
Marco T.: submitted the form (redacted functional note: "sensitivity to flashing/strobe lights, needs avoidance of direct exposure; requests private workspace while remediations occur"). DM'd Lina receipt.
Facilities: we can relocate the strobe or install a diffused cover to reduce flash intensity. permanent removal may require fire-safety sign-off; temporary private office available today. i'll schedule an inspection within 48h.
Aisha (Eng Manager): Facilities, please prioritize the inspection. Marco, i'll update the on-site seating map and block a private office for 2 weeks. we'll document this as temporary pending remediation.
Marco T.: appreciate it. one other concern: my tickets reference a customer-facing incident that triggered the panel. worried the incident log will mention "accommodation" or health details when shared with stakeholders. can we ensure only necessary teams see the accommodation note?
Lina (People Ops): good question — People Ops will document the accommodation in the private ledger only. incident postmortems and public logs should not include health or accommodation details. we can add a short manager-facing note on the private manager doc: "Temporary workspace adjustment for health reasons" without specifics. Legal can confirm wording.
Legal Counsel: confirm: redact any health specifics from postmortems. you may document operational impact (e.g., "employee relocated temporarily due to sensitivity to visual alarm") but avoid medical terminology. we'll review any external communications before release.
peopleops-bot: AC-2040-901 status changed: intake -> in-progress.
Marco T.: quick operational ask: while private office is in effect, i'll need access to the team's whiteboard notes and async summaries. can we add a requirement that team owners post meeting notes within 24h?
Aisha (Eng Manager): yes — we'll add a lightweight notes habit: brief bullets in the meeting thread and attach to the ticket. also will set up a camera-free shared doc.
Facilities: inspection scheduled for 2025-09-03 10:00. we'll test a diffused cover and measure lux/flicker metrics. if safety rules prevent removal, we'll propose an alternate alarm topology that keeps audible alarm but reduces strobe intensity in occupied zones.
Marco T.: sounds good. timeline okay. thanks for the quick help.
Lina (People Ops): summary of next steps:
``
1) People Ops confirms AC-2040-901 (documented) and notifies manager + Facilities
2) Facilities inspects and applies temporary mitigation (private office + diffused cover) within 48h/inspection window
3) Legal reviews any external incident comms to ensure no medical info disclosed
4) Manager ensures notes/async summaries for access and schedules 30-day check-in
```
Lina (People Ops): Marco, we'll follow up after the inspection and update the case. reach out via DM if you need immediate help. all health info here remains confidential. :lock: 
peopleops-bot: AC-2040-901 comment added by Lina (People Ops): "temporary workspace reassignment in place; facilities inspection scheduled"
Marco T.: thanks everyone — relief to have a concrete plan. :heart:
